title: Home
summary: MelonUI is a C# library for building console user interfaces. You can create pages and controls in C#, or use MXML, an XML-based markup language, to describe the UI in a file.
text: About The library is built around UIElement, the base class used by each control. ConsoleWindowManager handles displaying the UI and processing input, while your application provides the data and the methods called by the controls. C# and MXML use the same controls and element tree, so you can choose the approach that works best for your application. You can also load an MXML page and access its elements from C#. Features Built-in Controls: Text input, menus, buttons, progress bars, color pickers, and layout containers are included. MXML: Pages can be written in markup and recompiled while the application is running. If an edit fails to compile, the previous page is kept. Data Binding: Controls can read and update properties on your application objects, and call methods when the user interacts with them. Custom Controls: You can derive from UIElement and use the binding generator to add your own properties. Keyboard Controls: The window handles focus navigation, while individual controls handle editing and selection. Get Started Using MelonUI See the Quick Start Guide for setting up an application and creating your first page. C# and MXML For example, these two declarations create the same text input: C# Example C# Copy var page = new MUIPage { ShowBorder = false }; page.Children.Add( new TextBox { Label = Display name , Text = Melon listener , Width = 42 , Height = 5 }); MXML Example MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBox Label= Display name Text= Melon listener Width= 42 Height= 5 / /MUIPage Example Output: ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │Display name │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │Melon listener │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ Guides There are guides on how the different parts of MelonUI work and how to use them: Layout and Styling How to position elements, divide a page into cells, and change its colors. Managing Elements How to add, remove, reuse and dispose controls. ConsoleWindowManager How to run a window and update its UI from other threads. Focus and Keyboard Controls How focus moves between controls and how input is handled. Popups and Dialogs How to open a popup and handle its lifetime. MXML Guide How to write, load and update markup pages. Data Binding How to connect controls to your application data. Developing Custom Controls If the built-in controls do not cover what you need, you can create a class that derives from UIElement. See the Custom Controls Guide for a complete example, and the Binding Generator documentation for adding bindable properties. Reference Documentation The Controls Overview lists the built-in elements with C# and MXML examples. The API Reference also includes the supporting types, such as MenuItem, WorkItem and the binding classes. MelonUI targets .NET 10. The optional MelonUI.Shaders library contains the GPU controls; it is not needed for a normal console UI. Build instructions and platform information are in Building MelonUI .

title: Quick Start
summary: In this guide, we'll set up a console application and create a simple page with a text input, button and status message. After that, we'll create a similar page using MXML.
text: Prerequisites .NET SDK: .NET 10. Development Environment: Visual Studio or another C# IDE. The commands below also work from a terminal. MelonUI Source: A local checkout of the MelonUI repository. Interactive Terminal: Running the window requires console input and output. Use CaptureText when you only need an offline render. 1. Create the Application Create a console project and add a reference to MelonUI: Command Line Copy dotnet new console -n HelloMelon -f net10.0 dotnet add HelloMelon reference /path/to/MelonUI/MelonUI/MelonUI.csproj Replace the reference path with the location of your checkout. For example, on Windows this might be D:/Documents/GitHub/MelonUI/MelonUI/MelonUI.csproj. The project reference will also restore the Pastel and Wcwidth dependencies. 2. Create the Page Let's make the page display a name field and a button. When the user presses the button, we'll show a greeting below it. Add QuickStart.cs to your project with the following code: QuickStart.cs Copy using MelonUI.Base; using MelonUI.Default; using MelonUI.Managers; namespace MelonUI.Docs; public static class QuickStart { // Call this from Program.cs: await QuickStart.RunAsync(); public static async Task RunAsync() { await using var window = new ConsoleWindowManager { Title = Hello, MelonUI }; window.Elements.Add(CreatePage()); window.RegisterKeyboardControl(ConsoleKey.Escape, window.Stop, Quit ); await window.RunAsync(); } public static MUIPage CreatePage() { var status = new TextBlock { Text = Ready , Y = 8 , Height = 1 , ShowBorder = false }; var input = new TextBox { Label = Your name , Text = Melon listener , Width = 42 , Height = 5 }; var save = new Button { Text = Say hello , Y = 5 , Width = 42 , Height = 3 }; save.OnPressed = () = status.Text = $ Hello, {input.Text}! ; var page = new MUIPage { ShowBorder = false , Children = { input, save, status } }; return page; } } Replace the contents of Program.cs with: Program.cs Copy await MelonUI.Docs.QuickStart.RunAsync(); Understanding the Code ConsoleWindowManager: Manages the console window and runs the input/render loop. MUIPage.Children: Holds the controls on the page. Each control is added once. TextBox: Contains the name entered by the user. The label requires a height of 5 rows when a border is shown. Button.OnPressed: Updates the status TextBlock using the current input value. Y: Sets the vertical position. MUIPage does not automatically stack its children. RunAsync: Runs until Stop is called or the cancellation token is cancelled. 3. Run and Test Command Line Copy dotnet run --project HelloMelon You should see a page like this: Example Output: ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │Your name │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │Melon listener │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ [ Say hello ] Ready Enter a name in the TextBox. Press Tab to focus the Say hello button. Press Enter. The status should change to Hello, followed by the name you entered. Press Escape to stop the window and restore the console. 4. Create an MXML Page The same controls can be declared in MXML. Save Settings.mxml in your application project: Settings.mxml Copy MUIPage MxmlVersion= 1 ShowBorder= false TextBox Name= Name Label= Display name Text= {App.Name} Width= 42 Height= 5 / Button Text= Save changes OnPressed= {App.Save} Y= 5 Width= 42 Height= 3 Button.OnPressed Show Target= Saved Focus= false / /Button.OnPressed /Button TextBlock Name= Saved Text= {App.Status} Y= 8 Height= 1 IsVisible= false ShowBorder= false / /MUIPage Add the following ItemGroup inside your .csproj so the file is copied beside the executable: HelloMelon.csproj Copy ItemGroup None Update= Settings.mxml CopyToOutputDirectory= PreserveNewest / /ItemGroup The App bindings refer to a SettingsModel object. Add this class to your project: SettingsModel.cs Copy using System.ComponentModel; using System.Drawing; using MelonUI.Default; namespace MelonUI.Docs; public sealed class SettingsModel : INotifyPropertyChanged { private string _name = Melon listener ; private string _status = Ready ; private Color _accent = Color.FromArgb( 18 , 171 , 239 ); public event PropertyChangedEventHandler? PropertyChanged; public float [] Peaks { get; } = [. 1f , . 3f , . 8f , . 5f , 1f , . 6f , . 2f , . 4f ]; public string Name { get = _name; set { if (_name == value) return ; _name = value; Changed(nameof(Name)); } } public string Status { get = _status; private set { _status = value; Changed(nameof(Status)); } } public Color Accent { get = _accent; set { _accent = value; Changed(nameof(Accent)); } } public void Save() = Status = $ Saved {Name} ; public void Submit( string text, TextBox input) = Status = $ Hello, {text} ; public void PreviewColor(Color color) = Accent = color; public void SaveColor(Color color) = Status = $ Accent #{color.R:X2}{color.G:X2}{color.B:X2} ; public void OpenFile( string path) = Status = $ Opened {System.IO.Path.GetFileName(path)} ; private void Changed( string property) = PropertyChanged?.Invoke( this , new (property)); } Now add the code that loads the page and registers the model: MxmlStart.cs Copy using MelonUI.Base; using MelonUI.Managers; namespace MelonUI.Docs; public static class MxmlStart { // Pass the full path of Settings.mxml, or copy it beside your executable. public static async Task RunAsync( string filePath) { await using var window = new ConsoleWindowManager { Title = Settings }; var model = new SettingsModel(); var page = new MUIPage(); page.BackendObjects.Add( App , model); if (!page.CompileFile(filePath)) throw new InvalidOperationException(page.GetSimpleCompilerDisplay()); window.Elements.Add(page); window.RegisterKeyboardControl(ConsoleKey.Escape, window.Stop, Quit ); await window.RunAsync(); } } To run this version, use the following in Program.cs: Program.cs Copy await MelonUI.Docs.MxmlStart.RunAsync( Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, Settings.mxml )); BackendObjects gives MXML access to the existing model. The page does not own that model, so recompiling the markup will not replace or dispose it. See the Data Binding Guide for more info. 5. Try the Live MXML Demo From the MelonUI checkout, you can run the demo to edit markup while viewing the result: Command Line Copy dotnet run --no-launch-profile --project MelonUIDemo -- --mxml On Windows, the demo creates a file and opens it in Notepad. Save your changes to recompile the page. If there is an error, it will be shown below the last working page. F5 recompiles manually, and Escape closes the preview. The file is kept in the system temp directory after exit. On other platforms, open the displayed path in your editor. Using Local Packages The current code can also build MelonUI 1.0.0 as a local NuGet package. From the repository, run: Command Line Copy pwsh ./scripts/Verify-Packages.ps1 dotnet nuget add source /path/to/MelonUI/artifacts/package-validation/feed --name MelonUI-local dotnet add HelloMelon package MelonUI --version 1.0.0 Keep nuget.org configured alongside the local source so dependencies can be restored. Use -CoreOnly with Verify-Packages.ps1 if you do not need the shader package. These commands create local packages; they do not publish a public NuGet release. The NuGet package includes the binding generator. If you are using project references and adding custom bindable fields, see the generator setup .

title: Controls Overview
summary: MelonUI includes controls for displaying information, handling input and arranging pages. The following pages describe how to use each control in C# and MXML, with examples of the output.
text: Using Controls in C# The C# examples use these namespaces: C# Copy using MelonUI.Base; using MelonUI.Default; using MelonUI.Enums; using System.Drawing; Each example creates a control variable. Add it to Children on a page, or Elements on the window. MXML automatically resolves core types. Examples using App bindings refer to the SettingsModel class in the Data Binding guide. Pages MUIPage The MUIPage class is used to group UI elements into a page. You can add elements in C# through Children, or use MXML to load the page from a file. Text and Input TextBlock The TextBlock control displays text in the console. It supports word wrapping, text alignment, and inline colors, making it useful for labels, descriptions, and status messages. TextBox The TextBox control allows users to enter and edit text. You can use it for single-line input, multiline input, or hidden input such as a password. ColorPicker The ColorPicker control allows users to edit the red, green and blue values of a color. It shows the original color alongside the current color, so changes can be previewed before they are saved. RgbColorPicker The RgbColorPicker class provides the ColorPicker control under a name that makes its RGB behavior explicit. It uses the same properties, keyboard controls and events. FilePicker The FilePicker control allows users to browse for a file or directory. It keeps its own current directory, so using the picker does not change the working directory of your application. Buttons and Menus Button The Button control displays an action that the user can select. When the button is activated, it calls the method assigned to OnPressed. ButtonPanel The ButtonPanel control arranges buttons into an action bar. Buttons that do not fit are placed in an overflow menu, so the panel can still be used in a smaller console window. OptionsMenu The OptionsMenu control displays a list of choices. Each choice is a MenuItem containing its label, callback and enabled state. OverflowMenu The OverflowMenu class is an OptionsMenu that displays actions from a list of buttons. ButtonPanel uses it automatically when some of its buttons do not fit. Displaying Information ProgressBar The ProgressBar control displays progress for an operation. It can show a percentage and label, or use a loading animation when you do not know how much work remains. WorkLog The WorkLog control displays the progress of multiple jobs. Each job is a WorkItem with its own label, status, item counts and running time. Waveform The Waveform control displays peak amplitudes supplied by your application. It can also highlight how far playback has progressed through the data. Line The Line control draws a line between two points inside its own area. It can be used for dividers or simple horizontal, vertical and diagonal drawing. FPSCounter The FPSCounter control shows how many frames the window is actually presenting. It subscribes to the window when attached and removes that subscription when detached. Layout Containers GridContainer The GridContainer control divides its area into rows and columns. Each row can have a different number of columns, allowing you to build layouts without assigning a position to every control. QueueContainer The QueueContainer control displays the first visible element in a queue, with a small stack behind it to show that more elements are waiting. Other Controls You can also build a custom UIElement , or use the optional shader controls . The output examples are plain text, so they do not show the color of a rendered frame.

title: Layout and Styling
summary: Every UIElement has position, size and color properties. These are used by the window and its containers to calculate where each element is drawn.
text: Position and Size X / Y: The offset inside the parent's content area. An empty value means 0. The value center can be used to center a position. Width / Height: A number of console cells or a percentage of the available space. Both default to 100%. MinWidth / MaxWidth: The minimum and maximum horizontal size. MinHeight and MaxHeight apply to the vertical size. XYAlignment: The position used to anchor the control, such as TopLeft, BottomLeft or Centered. ActualX / ActualY / ActualWidth / ActualHeight: The calculated position and size after layout. Percentages are calculated from the space offered by the parent. They do not support expressions such as calc() or 100% - 2. Creating a Page Layout MUIPage does not place children below each other automatically. If two children use the same position, they will overlap. You can set X and Y yourself, or use a GridContainer to split the space into cells. For example, this page adds a heading, a two-column grid and a status message: C# Copy var page = new MUIPage { ShowBorder = false }; page.Children.Add( new TextBlock { Text = Library , Height = 1 , ShowBorder = false }); var grid = new GridContainer( 1 , false , 2 ) { Y = 1 , Height = 80% }; grid.AddElement( new TextBlock { Text = Albums }, 0 , 0 ); grid.AddElement( new TextBlock { Text = Artists }, 0 , 1 ); page.Children.Add(grid); page.Children.Add( new TextBlock { Text = Ready , Height = 1 , XYAlignment = Alignment.BottomLeft, ShowBorder = false }); GridContainer can use a different number of columns on each row. This is how a grid itself may look: Example Output: ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │┌──────────────────┐┌──────────────────┐│ ││Albums ││Artists ││ │└──────────────────┘└──────────────────┘│ │┌──────────────────────────────────────┐│ ││Now playing ││ ││ ││ │└──────────────────────────────────────┘│ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ The output above shows the grid control, rather than the entire heading/status example. Each child keeps its requested size within its assigned cell. Borders and Content Size A border uses one cell on each side of a control. This means a bordered TextBox needs 3 rows for one line of input, or 5 rows when it also has a label and separator: MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBox Height= 3 Width= 40 / TextBox Label= Name Y= 3 Height= 5 Width= 40 / /MUIPage TextAlignment controls the text inside a TextBlock, while XYAlignment controls the position of the whole element. GetAbsolutePosition can be used when you need the position relative to the console rather than the parent. Colors Foreground / Background: The normal text and background colors. A transparent background preserves what is underneath it. FocusedForeground / FocusedBackground: Colors used by controls for their focused state. BorderColor / FocusedBorderColor: The normal and focused border colors. MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBlock Text= Library ready Foreground= #50D282 Background= #202820 Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / /MUIPage MXML colors can be named colors, hex values such as #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB, or comma-separated RGB/ARGB bytes. Drawing Order Z controls the drawing order of siblings. Focusing an element does not change that order. Use BringToFront or SendToBack when you need to change which sibling is drawn last. Text is measured using console cell widths. Combining characters, emoji and other complex text can still depend on the terminal and font being used.

title: UIElement
summary: UIElement is the base class for all MelonUI controls. It provides the common properties for layout, styling, focus, data binding and element lifetime.
text: Common Properties Name / UID: Name is used for looking up an element. UID identifies a particular instance and does not change. Children / Parent / ParentWindow: The elements owned by this element and the page/window it belongs to. Ownership is managed through the collections. IsVisible / IsEnabled: Controls display and availability. IsEffectivelyVisible and IsEffectivelyEnabled also include the parent state. ConsiderForFocus / TabIndex: Controls whether the element is included in focus navigation and its order among siblings. IsFocused is managed by the window. LockControls: Prevents the control from responding to its normal input. EnableCaching: Allows the rendered buffer to be reused until the element changes. Common Methods Find T / FindById: Looks up a descendant by its name or UID. Remove: Detaches the element without destroying it. RequestRemove can queue this on the UI thread. Dispose: Removes the element and permanently cleans up its children, bindings and resources. Invalidate: Requests a new render for the element and its parents. SetBinding / RemoveBinding: Adds or removes a binding for a property. TryHandleKey / RegisterKeyboardControl: Handles input or registers a control-specific shortcut. Creating a Derived Class UIElement is abstract. To create a control, derive from it and implement RenderContent: C# Copy public partial class Label : MelonUI.Base.UIElement { [MelonUI.Attributes.Binding] private string _text = Hello ; public Label() { Height = 1 ; ShowBorder = false ; ConsiderForFocus = false ; } protected override void RenderContent(MelonUI.Base.ConsoleBuffer buffer) { var a = ContentRect; if (a.Width 0 a.Height 0 ) buffer.WriteString(a.X, a.Y, Text, Foreground, Background); } } The base Render method prepares the buffer and draws the border. RenderContent draws inside that buffer. See the Custom Controls Guide for a complete example with input handling and generated properties. Updating the Display Generated UI properties invalidate their element when changed. If you change other state that affects drawing, call Invalidate yourself. An animated control can set EnableCaching=false so it is rendered continuously. UIElement owns its Children collection, but it does not automatically draw the children. A container must lay out and combine their buffers. Use MUIPage if you only need normal page composition. API Reference The following members are declared by MelonUI.Base.UIElement . title: Managing Elements
summary: Elements are added through a page's Children collection or the window's Elements collection. Each element can only belong to one owner at a time.
text: Adding and Removing Elements Removing an element and disposing it are separate operations. Removing it allows you to keep the object and use it again, for example in a cache: C# Copy var card = new TextBlock { Text = Cached result }; first.Children.Add(card); card.Remove(); // detached, still usable second.Children.Add(card); // one owner at a time card.IsVisible = false ; // hidden, still owned card.Dispose(); // detached and permanently destroyed Add: Attaches an element that is not currently owned or disposed. Duplicate ownership and cycles are rejected. Remove / Clear: Detaches elements without disposing them. You are responsible for cleaning them up if they are no longer needed. IsVisible=false: Hides the element while keeping it attached and preserving its state. Dispose: Detaches the element and releases its resources. Calling it again is safe, but the element cannot be reused afterwards. Window Disposal: Stops the window and disposes roots that are still attached. Detached elements remain your responsibility. Removing from Another Thread When the window is running, RequestRemove can be called to queue removal on the UI thread: C# Copy element.RequestRemove(); The request applies to the current attachment. If the element or one of its parents is detached and reused before the request runs, the old request is ignored. RequestRemove does not dispose the element. Like other queued work, a new request is rejected while the window is stopping. Lifetime Methods Custom controls can override these methods to manage subscriptions and resources: OnAttachedToWindow: Subscribe to the current window and start window-specific work. OnDetachedFromWindow: Remove those subscriptions and stop window-specific work, while keeping the element reusable. OnChildAdded / OnChildRemoved: Update any layout or tracking information held by a container. DisposeCore: Permanently release resources owned by the element. Call the base implementation when extending an existing container. Keep these methods synchronous and avoid throwing during cleanup. Bindings managed by MelonUI suspend on detach and resume on reattachment; event subscriptions you add yourself need your own cleanup.

title: ConsoleWindowManager
summary: ConsoleWindowManager manages the console session, root elements, input and rendering. It runs the UI on one thread, so changes to attached controls need to happen on that thread.
text: Running the Window C# Copy await using var window = new ConsoleWindowManager { Title = Melon , TargetFrameRate = 60 }; window.Elements.Add( new MUIPage()); window.RegisterKeyboardControl(ConsoleKey.Escape, window.Stop, Quit ); await window.RunAsync(cancellationToken); Creating a window does not change the terminal. RunAsync starts the loop and completes after it stops and restores the terminal. Run is available if you need a blocking call instead. Do not start another run while one is already active. Title sets the console window or terminal title where supported. It does not add a heading to the UI. Headings and status messages should be normal controls. Updating the UI from Other Threads Use Post or InvokeAsync to change attached controls from background work: C# Copy // RunAsync must already be active. window.Post(() = status.Text = Scanning… ); await window.InvokeAsync(() = progress.ProgressValue = 0.65f ); Post(Action): Queues an action without waiting for it. Unhandled errors use the window's exception event. InvokeAsync(Action): Queues an action and returns a task you can await. An exception in the action faults that task. CheckAccess: Reports whether the current thread is allowed to access the UI. These methods are only available while RunAsync is active and the window has not started stopping. Stop your background producers before disposing the window. Keep the queued action short. Do file access, network requests and other slow work outside it. An async lambda passed as an Action becomes async void, so it should not be used to represent awaited background work. Window Events Updating: Called for recurring UI updates at the configured rate. Keep handlers short. FrameRendered: Called when a frame is actually presented. FrameNumber is the current sequence number. UnhandledException: Reports unexpected posted, keyboard and render/update callback errors. TargetFrameRate is the target update rate. It does not guarantee that every update writes a new frame; an unchanged cached frame may not be presented again. Example: Reloading an MXML File This example assumes the window is running and the page and status control are already attached: C# Copy var markup = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path, token); await window.InvokeAsync(() = { status.Text = page.Compile(markup, path) ? Compiled : page.GetSimpleCompilerDisplay(); }); The file is read before the UI action is queued. Compile returns false for invalid markup, leaving the previous page in place. A failure to read the file is a separate error for the application to handle. Handling Errors C# Copy window.UnhandledException += (_, e) = { // Log the exception using your application s logger. // Set e.Handled = true only if the application can safely continue. }; If an unexpected error is not handled, RunAsync faults after terminal cleanup. InvokeAsync actions report their errors through their own returned task. Do not write directly to Console while the UI is running. Use a TextBlock, a log control, or your application's logger instead. Capturing the UI CaptureText can compose the normal window without running an interactive terminal: C# Copy string output = window.CaptureText(width: 80 , height: 24 ); Give explicit dimensions when capturing before RunAsync. During a run, capture on the UI thread. Password fields are masked unless includeSensitive=true is explicitly supplied. You can also render a single element directly: C# Copy using var page = new MUIPage { Height = 5 , Width = 32 , ShowBorder = true }; page.Children.Add( new TextBlock { Text = Captured without a terminal , Height = 1 , ShowBorder = false }); page.CalculateLayout( 0 , 0 , 32 , 5 ); string text = page.Render().Screenshot(keepColor: false ); API Reference The following members are declared by MelonUI.Managers.ConsoleWindowManager . title: Focus and Keyboard Controls
summary: MelonUI sends input to the focused control first. If the control does not handle a key, it is passed to its parents and then to the window shortcuts.
text: Default Keyboard Controls Tab / Shift+Tab: Moves forward or backward through eligible controls. TabIndex orders siblings, followed by insertion order; traversal through containers is depth first. Alt+Arrows: Moves focus using the displayed positions of the controls. Alt+Backtick: Cycles focus. Hold Shift to reverse the direction. Normal Arrows: Are handled by the focused control, such as moving a text cursor or selecting a menu item. Hidden, disabled, detached, fully clipped and zero-content-size elements are skipped. ButtonPanel is one focus stop, while QueueContainer only exposes the current card. Focusing an Element C# Copy var name = page.Find TextBox ( Name ); if (name is not null ) window.Focus(name); Find returns null when the name is missing. It throws if the name is ambiguous or the type does not match. Use a page-scoped lookup when different pages contain elements with the same name. Focus does not change Z order. BringToFront and SendToBack are separate operations. Focusing a nonfocusable container selects an eligible child when one is available. Adding a Shortcut C# Copy window.RegisterKeyboardControl(ConsoleKey.S, Save, Save , requireControl: true ); Save should be a short method with no parameters. Normal shortcut registrations match modifiers exactly. A KeyboardControl.Wildcard predicate can choose which keys and modifiers to accept. EnableGlobalControls controls window shortcuts, and EnableSystemFocusControls controls built-in focus navigation. Neither property disables normal text editing. Handling Input in a Custom Control C# Copy public override bool TryHandleKey(ConsoleKeyInfo key) { if (LockControls || !IsEffectivelyVisible || !IsEffectivelyEnabled) return false ; if ( base .TryHandleKey(key)) return true ; if (key.Key != ConsoleKey.Enter || key.Modifiers != 0 ) return false ; // Handle Enter here. return true ; } Return true only for keys that your control handles. Calling base.TryHandleKey allows registered control-specific shortcuts to run. Unhandled keys can then continue through the normal input chain. Focus in Popups The top active modal keeps focus and input inside it. Background window shortcuts are suppressed, and an unhandled Escape closes the popup. Closing, hiding or disabling a modal restores an eligible previous focus target. See Popups and Dialogs for more info.

title: Popups and Dialogs
summary: A popup uses a normal UI element as its content. ShowPopup registers it with the window and returns a handle for closing or disposing it.
text: Example: Color Selection Let's create a color picker that previews changes and closes when the user confirms or cancels. Call this code on the UI thread, with an attached preview TextBlock: C# Copy var picker = new RgbColorPicker { Width = 70% , Height = 8 , XYAlignment = Alignment.Centered }; picker.BeginEdit(preview.Foreground); var dialog = window.ShowPopup(picker); picker.ColorChanged += color = preview.Foreground = color; picker.Confirmed += _ = dialog.Dispose(); picker.Cancelled += color = { preview.Foreground = color; dialog.Dispose(); }; Example Output: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ R [─────────────█─────────────────────────────] 080│ │ G [───────────────────────────────────█───────] 210│ │ B [─────────────────────█─────────────────────] 130│ │Old #50D282 │ │New #50D282 ███ │ │↑↓ channel ←→ value Shift:10 Enter:save Esc:canc│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Understanding the Code BeginEdit: Sets the color that will be restored if the user cancels. ShowPopup: Displays and focuses the picker as a modal. ColorChanged: Updates the preview while the user edits. Confirmed: Keeps the chosen color and disposes the dialog. Cancelled: Receives the restored color, updates the preview and disposes the dialog. Popup Lifetime Close(): Detaches the popup content so it can be reused, and restores an eligible previous focus target. Calling Close again is safe. Dispose(): Closes the registration and permanently disposes its content. IsOpen: Reports whether this handle still owns its popup attachment. ShowPopup(content, isModal: false): Creates a nonmodal popup. Keep the handle until the dialog is finished. A using statement in a method that immediately returns would dispose the popup as soon as that method ends. Opening a Popup from MXML MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false Button Text= Choose accent OnPressed= {App.OpenColorDialog} / /MUIPage App.OpenColorDialog is a public backend method that creates the popup using the C# code above. MXML Show and Hide actions change existing elements; they do not register a modal popup.

title: MXML Guide
summary: MXML is an XML-based markup language used to create MelonUI pages. It describes the same elements, properties and callbacks that you use when building the UI in C#.
text: Page Structure The root element must be MUIPage. You can set MxmlVersion="1" to explicitly select the language version; unsupported versions fail compilation. Settings.mxml Copy MUIPage MxmlVersion= 1 ShowBorder= false TextBox Name= Name Label= Display name Text= {App.Name} Width= 42 Height= 5 / Button Text= Save changes OnPressed= {App.Save} Y= 5 Width= 42 Height= 3 Button.OnPressed Show Target= Saved Focus= false / /Button.OnPressed /Button TextBlock Name= Saved Text= {App.Status} Y= 8 Height= 1 IsVisible= false ShowBorder= false / /MUIPage Core types in MelonUI.Base and MelonUI.Default are available without namespace declarations. Attributes set public CLR properties. Normal XML escaping applies, such as amp; for an ampersand and #10; for a line break inside an attribute. Compiling a Page Register any application objects that the markup uses, then compile the file: C# Copy var page = new MUIPage(); page.BackendObjects.Add( App , new SettingsModel()); if (!page.CompileFile( Settings.mxml )) throw new InvalidOperationException(page.GetSimpleCompilerDisplay()); BackendObjects refers to existing objects that your application owns. The compiler does not dispose those objects. Backends declared in markup with Backends="Alias=TypeName" are created when needed and are owned by their page scope. A disposable backend created this way is cleaned up after failure, replacement or final page disposal. Child pages inherit the available aliases. New declarations remain inside the child scope. Static backend classes can also be referenced without constructing an instance. Children and Property Elements MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false MUIPage Name= Details Width= 50% MUIPage.Children TextBlock Text= Nested page Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / /MUIPage.Children /MUIPage OptionsMenu X= 50% Width= 50% OptionsMenu.Options MenuItem Option= Albums / MenuItem Option= Artists / /OptionsMenu.Options /OptionsMenu /MUIPage UI elements belong to the element containing them, in declaration order. Data objects such as MenuItem and WorkItem go inside an explicit collection property instead of Children. Property elements use Owner.Property, where Owner is the current type or one of its base types. Collections can contain one or more objects. A scalar property element can contain text or a binding. Including Other Pages MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false MUIPage Name= Settings Source= pages/settings.mxml Width= 60% / Button Text= Focus name X= 60% Width= 40% Button.OnPressed Focus Target= Settings/Name / /Button.OnPressed /Button /MUIPage Relative includes are resolved beside the file containing them. Attributes on the include element override settings from the included page. MXMLFilePath is also accepted as an include alias. Compile(text, sourcePath) compiles the text you supply without rereading the file. sourcePath provides the directory used for relative includes. Without a source path, CompilerOptions.BaseDirectory is used, followed by the process working directory. Compiling never changes that working directory. Recursive includes and documents exceeding the configured size/depth limits are reported as errors. Element Names Names must be unique within the nearest page, including ordinary nested containers. A nested MUIPage creates a new scope. Name: Looks for an element inside the current page scope. Settings/Name: Looks for Name inside the named Settings child page. .: Refers to the current page. Action targets can refer to elements declared later in the file. They are resolved after the page has been parsed. Custom Types and Constructors C# Copy page.CompilerOptions.Assemblies.Add( typeof (Badge).Assembly); page.CompilerOptions.Namespaces.Add( MelonUI.Docs ); page.CompilerOptions.Factories.Add( typeof (GridContainer), () = new GridContainer( 2 , false , 2 , 1 )); Normally the compiler uses a public parameterless constructor. You can register a factory when a type needs constructor arguments or services from the application. The factory must return a new, unattached and undisposed instance of the requested type. Assemblies, Namespaces and Backends declarations in MXML are handled in phases, so their attribute order does not matter. Fully qualified names or CLR XML namespace prefixes can be used when short type names would be ambiguous. Reloading MXML The compiler builds a new page before replacing the current one. This allows an application to keep showing a working UI while a file is being edited: C# Copy var markup = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path, token); await window.InvokeAsync(() = { status.Text = page.Compile(markup, path) ? Compiled : page.GetSimpleCompilerDisplay(); }); Compilation Fails: The current children, root settings, bindings and focus are kept. Read the diagnostics to show the error. Compilation Succeeds: Children are replaced and the old owned elements and bindings are disposed. A uniquely named eligible focus target is restored. Root Properties: Properties included in the new markup replace their previous values. Omitted root settings remain unchanged. While the window is running, compile on the UI thread using Post or InvokeAsync. Read the file outside that action. Custom setters and lifetime methods should not throw or cause external changes during compilation; normal rollback cannot undo arbitrary application behavior. Notes MXML is intended for trusted application and plugin code. It can create registered classes, call backends and include local files, so it should not be treated as a sandbox for untrusted input. DTDs and external XML entities are prohibited. See Data Binding , MXML Actions , and Diagnostics and Troubleshooting for more information.

title: Data Binding
summary: Data binding connects an element property or callback to an object in your application. This allows controls to display and update data without manually copying every value between the model and UI.
text: Creating a Backend A backend can be a normal class with public properties and methods. This example uses INotifyPropertyChanged so the UI can be told when a value changes: SettingsModel.cs Copy using System.ComponentModel; using System.Drawing; using MelonUI.Default; namespace MelonUI.Docs; public sealed class SettingsModel : INotifyPropertyChanged { private string _name = Melon listener ; private string _status = Ready ; private Color _accent = Color.FromArgb( 18 , 171 , 239 ); public event PropertyChangedEventHandler? PropertyChanged; public float [] Peaks { get; } = [. 1f , . 3f , . 8f , . 5f , 1f , . 6f , . 2f , . 4f ]; public string Name { get = _name; set { if (_name == value) return ; _name = value; Changed(nameof(Name)); } } public string Status { get = _status; private set { _status = value; Changed(nameof(Status)); } } public Color Accent { get = _accent; set { _accent = value; Changed(nameof(Accent)); } } public void Save() = Status = $ Saved {Name} ; public void Submit( string text, TextBox input) = Status = $ Hello, {text} ; public void PreviewColor(Color color) = Accent = color; public void SaveColor(Color color) = Status = $ Accent #{color.R:X2}{color.G:X2}{color.B:X2} ; public void OpenFile( string path) = Status = $ Opened {System.IO.Path.GetFileName(path)} ; private void Changed( string property) = PropertyChanged?.Invoke( this , new (property)); } Register the instance before compiling: C# Copy page.BackendObjects.Add( App , model); Name can be read and written. Status has no public setter, so it is read-only to MXML. Save, Submit and the color/file methods are callbacks that controls can call. Binding Properties MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBox Text= {Binding Path=App.Name, Mode=TwoWay} Height= 3 / TextBlock Text= {Binding Path=App.Status, Mode=OneWay} Y= 3 Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / TextBlock Text= {Binding Path=App.Name, Mode=OneTime} Y= 4 Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / /MUIPage TwoWay: Reads and writes a public writable property. This is the default when the source has a public setter. OneWay: Reads the value without writing back. This is the default for read-only properties and methods. Trying to write through a OneWay binding throws an error. OneTime: Copies the value during compilation without installing a live binding. The shorter form {App.Name} selects the default mode. Bindings apply to the whole value; they do not evaluate arbitrary C# expressions or interpolate a binding into the middle of a string. Binding endpoints must be public properties, methods or events. Fields, indexers and private members are not supported. Callbacks and Events MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBox OnEnter= {App.Submit} Height= 5 / RgbColorPicker Y= 5 Height= 8 ColorValue= {App.Accent} ColorChanged= {App.PreviewColor} Confirmed= {App.SaveColor} / /MUIPage Callback methods must match the delegate or event signature. For example: C# Copy public void Submit( string text, TextBox input) { /* handle input */ } public void SaveColor(System.Drawing.Color color) { /* save the color */ } Delegate properties call compatible public methods or the current delegate value. CLR control events can call a backend handler. The reverse also works: a public control method can handle a backend event. Overloaded methods are resolved against the expected delegate signature. A background event is dispatched to the attached window's UI thread. Do not use async void callbacks as a substitute for awaited application work. Updating Bound Values INotifyPropertyChanged and INotifyCollectionChanged allow MelonUI to invalidate controls when their data changes. Nested paths are followed again when an intermediate object is replaced. For App.Profile.Name, notify Profile when replacing that object, and notify Name on its new instance when the name changes. Background notifications queue UI invalidation, but this does not make your model or ordinary lists thread-safe. Manage changes to shared state deliberately, normally on the UI thread. Plain/static sources and some nested paths use polling. Subscriptions suspend when a control is detached, resume once when it is attached again, and are released after replacement or disposal. Binding from C# C# Copy input.SetBinding(nameof(TextBox.Text), Binding.CreatePath(model, nameof(SettingsModel.Name), typeof ( string ))); input.Text = Ada ; // writes model.Name input.RemoveBinding(nameof(TextBox.Text)); CreatePath accepts the source instance, a member path and an optional target type. A Type can be supplied for static members. There are also constructors taking PropertyInfo, MethodInfo or EventInfo. Generated setters write through an installed binding. RemoveBinding removes and disposes that binding. Values and Conversion MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBlock Text= {}{literal braces} Foreground= #12ABEF Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / TextBlock Text= {Null} Y= 1 Height= 1 ShowBorder= false / Waveform WaveformData= {App.Peaks} Y= 2 Height= 7 / /MUIPage Conversions use invariant culture, so decimal values use a period. Supported values include primitives, enums, nullable values, Guid, TimeSpan, colors, compatible typed arrays and type converters. {Null}: Supplies null to a compatible reference or nullable property. {}: Escapes a literal opening brace. Arrays: Bind a typed array such as App.Peaks; a comma-separated string does not automatically create it. TypeExtensions: Register a host conversion with page.TypeExtensions[typeof(MyType)] when a custom type needs one. Errors from direct C# binding getters and setters remain visible to the application rather than silently using an old value.

title: MXML Actions
summary: MXML actions allow a callback to show, hide, focus or update elements without writing a separate method for each operation. Actions are validated during compilation and run in the order they are declared.
text: Example Usage MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false Button Text= Save OnPressed= {App.Save} Height= 3 Button.OnPressed Set Target= Result Property= Text Value= Saved / Show Target= Result Focus= false / /Button.OnPressed /Button TextBlock Name= Result Y= 3 Height= 1 ShowBorder= false IsVisible= false / /MUIPage Understanding the Code OnPressed: Calls App.Save first. Set: Changes the Result text to Saved. Show: Makes Result visible without moving focus. If the bound callback throws, later actions are not run. Repeated actions are allowed and keep their declaration order. Targets can be declared later in the file. Available Actions Show: Takes Target and an optional Focus value, which defaults to true. Hide: Takes Target. Toggle: Takes Target and an optional Focus value, which defaults to false. Focus: Takes Target. Set: Takes Target, Property and Value. The property and conversion are checked during compilation. Invoke: Takes Path, pointing to a public parameterless backend method. An Actions wrapper can be used to group actions. Blocks require a void-returning callback or event. Targets use the current page scope, with paths such as Settings/Name for named child pages. Actions from a replaced document will not operate on its detached or disposed targets. MXMLFlags For short sequences, MXMLFlags provides a compact version of the same actions: MXML Copy Button.OnPressed MXMLFlags= Show(Result:false),Hide(Editor),Toggle(Help),Focus(Name) / Place this property element inside a Button, with Result, Editor, Help and Name declared in its page. Commas or semicolons separate the flags. Show and Toggle accept an optional :true/:false or second comma argument. Flags append after an existing callback rather than replacing it. Unknown flags, empty arguments and invalid boolean values are compilation errors. Notes Declare UI elements normally, then use Show or Hide to change them. UI declarations cannot be embedded inside a callback. To create a modal popup, call ConsoleWindowManager.ShowPopup from a backend method.

title: Creating Custom Controls
summary: In this guide, we'll create a UIElement-derived control with a caption, active state and keyboard callback. We'll then use it in both C# and MXML.
text: Prerequisites A .NET 10 project referencing MelonUI. The binding generator referenced by the project containing your annotated fields. See Binding Generator for setup. A basic understanding of the UIElement properties and the ConsoleBuffer . 1. Create the Control Class Add the following Badge class to your project: Badge.cs Copy using MelonUI.Base; using System.Globalization; using System.Text; namespace MelonUI.Docs; // A complete custom control: generated properties, bounded drawing and keyboard input. public partial class Badge : UIElement { [MelonUI.Attributes.Binding] private string _caption = Ready ; [MelonUI.Attributes.Binding] private bool _active; [MelonUI.Attributes.Binding] private Action? _onActivated; public Badge() { Height = 3 ; Width = 28 ; } protected override void RenderContent(ConsoleBuffer buffer) { var area = ContentRect; if (area.Width == 0 || area.Height == 0 ) return ; var color = Active ? FocusedForeground : Foreground; var text = $ {(Active ? ● : ○ )} {Caption} ; var visible = new StringBuilder(); var elements = StringInfo.GetTextElementEnumerator(text); int remaining = area.Width; while (elements.MoveNext()) { var next = elements.GetTextElement(); int width = ConsoleBuffer.GetTextElementWidth(next); if (width remaining) break; visible.Append(next); remaining -= width; } buffer.WriteString(area.X, area.Y, visible.ToString(), color, Background); } public override bool TryHandleKey(ConsoleKeyInfo key) { if (LockControls || !IsEffectivelyVisible || !IsEffectivelyEnabled) return false ; if ( base .TryHandleKey(key)) return true ; if (key.Key != ConsoleKey.Enter || key.Modifiers != 0 ) return false ; Active = !Active; OnActivated?.Invoke(); return true ; } } Understanding the Code partial class: Allows the binding generator to add properties to the class. Binding Fields: Generate Caption, Active and OnActivated. These properties use the base binding and invalidation behavior. ContentRect: Gives the usable area inside the border. A bordered control with Height=3 has one content row. RenderContent: Draws the active marker and caption, clipping by text elements so long text does not overwrite the border. TryHandleKey: Toggles Active on Enter, calls OnActivated, and returns true to mark the key as handled. After Enter changes the active state, the output looks like this: Example Output: ┌──────────────────────────┐ │● Ready │ └──────────────────────────┘ 2. Add the Control in C# C# Copy var badge = new MelonUI.Docs.Badge { Caption = Ready , Active = false }; badge.OnActivated = () = status.Text = badge.Active ? Active : Inactive ; page.Children.Add(badge); The generated setters already invalidate the element. You do not need to call Invalidate again after assigning Caption or Active. State that is not handled by those setters should invalidate the control explicitly. 3. Use the Control in MXML Register the assembly and namespace before compiling the page: C# Copy page.CompilerOptions.Assemblies.Add( typeof (MelonUI.Docs.Badge).Assembly); page.CompilerOptions.Namespaces.Add( MelonUI.Docs ); MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false Badge Caption= Custom control Active= true OnActivated= {App.Save} / /MUIPage App.Save is a public parameterless method on your registered backend. If two types have the same short name, use a CLR XML namespace prefix. For this example that would be xmlns:docs="clr-namespace:MelonUI.Docs;assembly=MelonUI.DocsExamples", followed by docs:Badge. Replace the assembly name with the name of your own assembly. If the control needs constructor arguments, register a factory through CompilerOptions.Factories. 4. Manage Subscriptions and Resources A control may be removed and reused without being disposed. Subscribe to window events while attached and remove those subscriptions when detached: C# Copy protected override void OnAttachedToWindow(ConsoleWindowManager window) { window.Updating += OnUpdate; base .OnAttachedToWindow(window); } protected override void OnDetachedFromWindow(ConsoleWindowManager window) { window.Updating -= OnUpdate; base .OnDetachedFromWindow(window); } // OnUpdate is a short EventHandler UiUpdateEventArgs . // DisposeCore releases permanent resources, then calls base.DisposeCore(). Stop or cancel window-specific work on detach, while keeping the object reusable. DisposeCore is for final resource cleanup. Keep lifetime methods synchronous and avoid throwing from them during cleanup. 5. Build and Test A control should be checked in more than its initial layout. Test the following: Small Sizes: One row, no content area, clipped layouts, nested parents and repeated resizing. Input: Modifier keys, disabled/hidden/locked state, unhandled keys, focus navigation and modals. Bindings: Property changes, callbacks, detach/reattach, document replacement and disposal. Drawing: Borders, transparent backgrounds, Unicode text and cache invalidation. Lifetime: Repeated reuse without duplicate subscriptions or abandoned background work. Custom containers also need to lay out and draw their children. If the standard page behavior is enough, derive from or use MUIPage instead.

title: Binding Generator
summary: The binding generator adds public binding-aware properties for annotated fields. This allows a custom control to expose properties to C# and MXML without writing the same getter and setter code for each one.
text: Setting Up the Generator The MelonUI NuGet package includes the analyzer. If you are using source project references, add an analyzer reference in the project that declares the annotated fields: MXML Copy ItemGroup ProjectReference Include= ../MelonUI/MelonUI.csproj / ProjectReference Include= ../MelonUIBindingGenerator/MelonUIBindingGenerator.csproj OutputItemType= Analyzer ReferenceOutputAssembly= false / /ItemGroup Adjust the paths relative to your .csproj. The generator targets netstandard2.0 because it runs as a build tool; MelonUI and the application target .NET 10. Example Usage Add the Binding attribute to a mutable instance field in a partial class: C# Copy public partial class Badge : UIElement { [MelonUI.Attributes.Binding] private string _caption = Ready ; // Add RenderContent as shown in the complete custom control example. } This generates a Caption property. Its behavior is equivalent to the following simplified code; you do not add this property yourself: C# Copy public string Caption { get = ( string )GetBoundValue(nameof(Caption), _caption)!; set = SetBoundValue(nameof(Caption), value, ref _caption); } Leading underscores are removed, then the first remaining letter is capitalized. For example, _caption becomes Caption, _IsVisible becomes IsVisible, and onActivated becomes OnActivated. Supported Fields and Classes Fields must be mutable instance fields. Static, readonly and const fields are not supported. The class and every containing class must be nonstatic partial classes. A generated property cannot share a name with another generated, existing or inherited property. Do not declare binding helper members that conflict with the generated helpers. UIElement already provides these methods. Multiple fields, nested/generic classes, qualified attributes and attribute aliases are supported. Classes in different namespaces can have the same short name. Using the fully qualified MelonUI.Attributes.Binding attribute avoids ambiguity with the MelonUI.Base.Binding class. MXML binds to the generated public property, not the field. Compiler Diagnostics Code Description MUIB001 The attribute was applied to an unsupported declaration. Use a mutable field rather than a property or event. MUIB002 The class or one of its containing classes is not a nonstatic partial class. MUIB003 The field is static, readonly or const, so it cannot be generated. MUIB004 The generated property name conflicts with an existing, inherited or generated member. MUIB005 The type declares reserved binding helpers. Remove the conflicting helpers or derive from UIElement. Using the Generator on Data Classes A non-UI partial data class can also receive IBindingHost storage. Generated setters support binding, but they do not automatically implement INotifyPropertyChanged. Add notifications yourself when you want consumers to be invalidated efficiently. If you install bindings directly on a non-UI object, remove them when they are no longer needed. UIElement normally handles that lifetime for its own bindings.

title: ConsoleBuffer
summary: ConsoleBuffer holds the characters and colors used to draw a control. A custom UIElement receives its buffer in RenderContent and writes into it using local coordinates.
text: Drawing Text and Cells C# Copy protected override void RenderContent(ConsoleBuffer buffer) { var a = ContentRect; if (a.Width == 0 || a.Height == 0 ) return ; buffer.FillRect(a.X, a.Y, a.Width, a.Height, , Foreground, Background); buffer.WriteString(a.X, a.Y, Ready , Foreground, Background); } ContentRect excludes the control's border. Drawing methods are bounded by the buffer, but you should also clip content to ContentRect if it must not overwrite the border. The Badge example shows text-element clipping. Drawing Methods SetPixel: Sets the character, foreground and background of a cell. WriteString / WriteStringWrapped: Writes a string directly or wraps it to a width. FillRect / DrawRect: Fills an area or draws a box. WriteBuffer: Combines a child buffer at a local position. respectBackground defaults to true. CreateSubBuffer: Creates a buffer from a bounded subregion. GetStringWidth / GetTextElementWidth: Measures best-effort terminal cell widths. Screenshot: Returns text output, with optional color escape sequences. The buffer indexer uses [row, column], while drawing methods use (x, y). ConsoleWindowManager handles presenting the frame; a custom control should not call RenderToConsole itself. Capturing a Render C# Copy using var page = new MUIPage { Height = 5 , Width = 32 , ShowBorder = true }; page.Children.Add( new TextBlock { Text = Captured without a terminal , Height = 1 , ShowBorder = false }); page.CalculateLayout( 0 , 0 , 32 , 5 ); string text = page.Render().Screenshot(keepColor: false ); The output examples in these docs use a 64 by 12 window capture, without ANSI colors. Trailing whitespace is removed. FilePicker's directory caption is replaced with /demo so it does not show a machine-specific path. Display widths and shaping for combining characters and emoji can still depend on the terminal and font. API Reference The following members are declared by MelonUI.Base.ConsoleBuffer . Constructors ConsoleBuffer(int width, int height) Properties ConsolePixel Item[int, int] { get; set; } ConsolePixel Item[int] { get; set; } int Height { get; } int Width { get; } UnixRenderer URenderer { get; } Win32Renderer WRenderer { get; } Fields ConsolePixel[] buffer Methods byte[] StructToBytes(ConsolePixel[] structure) ConsoleBuffer CreateSubBuffer(int x, int y, int width, int height) int GetCharWidth(char c) int GetStringWidth(string str) int GetTextElementWidth(string element) string Screenshot(bool keepColor) void Clear(Color background) void DrawRect(int x, int y, int width, int height, Color foreground, Color background) void FillRect(int x, int y, int width, int height, char c, Color foreground, Color background) void RenderToConsole(StreamWriter output, bool UsePlatformSpecificRenderer) void Resize(int newWidth, int newHeight) void SetPixel(int x, int y, char c, Color foreground, Color background, bool forceIsWide = false) void Write(int x, int y, ConsoleBuffer source) void WriteBuffer(int x, int y, ConsoleBuffer source, bool respectBackground = true) void WriteLines(int x, int y, IEnumerable string lines, Color foreground, Color background) void WriteLinesCentered(int startY, IEnumerable string lines, Color foreground, Color background) void WriteString(int x, int y, string text, Color foreground, Color background) void WriteStringCentered(int y, string text, Color foreground, Color background) void WriteStringWrapped(int x, int y, string text, int maxWidth, Color foreground, Color background) These signatures list public members from the current assembly. Nullable reference annotations and generic constraints are not reproduced here.

title: Diagnostics and Troubleshooting
summary: MelonUI reports build-time generator errors, MXML compilation errors and runtime UI errors separately. This page explains where to find those errors and some common causes.
text: MXML Compilation Errors C# Copy if (!page.Compile(markup, sourcePath)) { var result = page.CompilerFocusedMessage; // Code, SourcePath, MxmlLineNumber.Line / Position, Message, Severity status.Text = page.GetSimpleCompilerDisplay(maxWidth: 100 ); } CompilerMessages: All messages produced by the last compilation. CompilerFocusedMessage: The current result, including the source path and XML line/column. CompilationFinished: The elapsed compilation time. MXML / MXMLFilePath: The last successfully compiled document. A failed edit does not replace these. GetSimpleCompilerDisplay formats the messages without writing to the console. Common Problems Problem Things to Check Content is blank or overlapping Check X/Y, Height, visibility and the content space left by borders. Pages do not automatically stack children. A labeled TextBox has no input row Use Height= 5 or larger when a border is shown. A grid cell is out of range Register a GridContainer factory with the intended constructor row and column counts. A generated property is missing Check that the field is mutable, its class is partial, and the analyzer is referenced by that project. A bound value does not update Check the public property path, backend alias, notifications and any caching/polling requirements. An included file cannot be found Supply sourcePath or CompilerOptions.BaseDirectory. Includes are relative to the file containing them. Changing an attached control throws Queue the change with Post or InvokeAsync while RunAsync is active. Stop producers during shutdown. RunAsync requires an interactive terminal Avoid redirected input/output, or use CaptureText for headless rendering. FilePicker still shows the previous filter Call Refresh after changing Extensions. OpenGL initialization fails Call Init on the application main thread before awaiting RunAsync, and check graphics support. Runtime Errors Compile returns false for expected markup errors. Once the page is running, failures in callbacks or bindings use the normal runtime error handling. InvokeAsync faults its returned task. Unexpected posted, keyboard and frame/update errors reach UnhandledException and otherwise fault RunAsync after terminal cleanup. Only set Handled=true if the application can safely continue.

title: Building MelonUI
summary: MelonUI targets .NET 10, with the binding generator targeting netstandard2.0. The repository has separate build entry points for the full solution and the portable core.
text: Building and Running Tests Command Line Copy # Windows: full solution, including optional shaders and demos. dotnet build MelonUIDemo.sln -c Release --warnaserror dotnet run --project MelonUI.Tests -c Release --no-build -- --gpu --soak # Linux/macOS: core, generator and tests. dotnet build MelonUI.slnf -c Release --warnaserror dotnet run --project MelonUI.Tests -c Release --no-build -- --soak MelonUI.Tests is an executable regression runner rather than a dotnet test adapter. --soak runs 500 MXML reloads to check cleanup. --gpu adds a Windows hardware test. The full shader source build currently requires Windows because ComputeSharp's source generator invokes native Windows compiler APIs. Building Local Packages Command Line Copy pwsh ./scripts/Verify-Packages.ps1 pwsh ./scripts/Verify-Packages.ps1 -CoreOnly This script builds local 1.0.0 packages and checks them from separate application/plugin consumers. It does not publish to NuGet, create a Git tag or make a release. The core runtime depends on Pastel and Wcwidth. Its package includes the binding analyzer. MelonUI.Shaders has the optional graphics dependencies. Platform and Runtime Information Runtime: Normal untrimmed/JIT .NET 10. Reflection-based MXML and arbitrary plugins are not supported as trimming/NativeAOT deployments in 1.0. Platforms: Windows and Linux have been checked locally. Native macOS and more terminal/SSH environments still need hands-on testing. File Browsing: Local directory enumeration is synchronous and is not a sandbox. Text: Console widths are best-effort; some shaping depends on the terminal and font. Graphics: Optional controls have device and main-thread requirements. Normal controls do not need a GPU. Removed Prototypes: The image viewer, audio player, decoders and playback managers are not part of the core. Waveform takes peaks supplied by the host. The library uses the MIT license. See LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the repository for licensing and dependency notices. The docs describe the current source and local packages, rather than claiming that a public package release has been made. Building the Documentation From docs/site in the repository: Command Line Copy node scripts/prepare-examples.mjs dotnet run --project examples/DocsExamples.csproj -c Release -- . node scripts/build.mjs node scripts/check.mjs node scripts/serve.mjs There are no npm dependencies. The .NET example runner refreshes the API list and control output examples. The Node build creates static HTML in dist, which can be served by a static host, including from a subfolder. The guide index is content/guides.mjs, with individual guides in content/guides/. Control examples are in content/controls.mjs. See content/STYLE.md for the writing and layout conventions used by these docs.

title: Optional Shader Controls
summary: MelonUI.Shaders contains OpenGLShaderElement and ShaderDisplay. These are optional graphics controls and are not required for the normal console UI library.
text: OpenGLShaderElement OpenGLShaderElement renders a GLSL shader. Constructing or compiling the control does not create a graphics context. Call Init on the application main thread before awaiting the UI loop: C# Example C# Copy using MelonUI.Shaders; var shader = new OpenGLShaderElement { ShaderPath = effect.glsl }; page.Children.Add(shader); window.Elements.Add(page); shader.Init(); await window.RunAsync(); MXML Example MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false Assemblies= MelonUI.Shaders Namespaces= MelonUI.Shaders OpenGLShaderElement Name= Shader ShaderPath= effect.glsl / /MUIPage After compiling the MXML, use page.Find OpenGLShaderElement ("Shader")!.Init() before awaiting RunAsync. ShaderSource can supply the GLSL directly instead of a file. Shader file loading is separate from MXML includes; provide a host path that can be read. ErrorMessage describes initialization or rendering failures. Actual output depends on the shader, GPU and driver. The repository shader demo includes a complete shader and startup/resize checks. ShaderDisplay ShaderDisplay uses Windows/Direct3D compute. It allocates its resources when needed and displays its built-in gradient unless you supply another shader: C# Example C# Copy using MelonUI.Shaders; var display = new ShaderDisplay(); page.Children.Add(display); // Use UpdateShader T (texture = shader) to supply a typed ComputeSharp shader. MXML Example MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false Assemblies= MelonUI.Shaders Namespaces= MelonUI.Shaders ShaderDisplay Name= Compute / /MUIPage UpdateShader T takes a factory receiving ReadWriteTexture2D float4 . T must be a struct implementing IComputeShader and IComputeShaderDescriptor T . Check ErrorMessage when the device or shader cannot run. Lifetime and Testing Workers publish complete frames together with their dimensions. During resizing, the previous completed frame is clipped using its own size. Detach pauses reusable graphics activity, while final disposal joins workers and releases native resources. Command Line Copy dotnet run --no-launch-profile --project MelonUIDemo -- --shader --smoke

title: MUIPage
summary: The MUIPage class is used to group UI elements into a page. You can add elements in C# through Children, or use MXML to load the page from a file.
text: Properties and Methods Children : Contains the elements that belong to this page. An element can only belong to one page or window at a time. Compile / CompileFile : Builds the page from MXML and returns whether compilation succeeded. If it fails, the previous page is kept. BackendObjects : Contains application objects that MXML can use for data binding and callbacks. Add these before compiling the page. CompilerOptions : Allows you to register custom types, choose how they are created, and set the base directory and include limits. C# Example Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples. C# Copy var control = new MUIPage { ShowBorder = true , Height = 7 }; control.Children.Add( new TextBlock { Text = Library , ShowBorder = false , Height = 1 }); control.Children.Add( new Button { Text = Open library , Y = 2 , Height = 3 }); MXML Example MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= true Height= 7 TextBlock Text= Library ShowBorder= false Height= 1 / Button Text= Open library Y= 2 Height= 3 / /MUIPage Output Example Example Output: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │Library │ │ │ │ │ │ [ Open library ] │ │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Notes Each nested MUIPage has its own MXML name scope. You can use the same name in different pages, but names inside one page must be unique. Children are positioned using their X, Y, Width and Height settings. They are not automatically placed below each other. For a layout with rows and columns, use GridContainer. MUIPage does not receive focus itself. Focusing a page selects an eligible element inside it. The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement . title: TextBox
summary: The TextBox control allows users to enter and edit text. You can use it for single-line input, multiline input, or hidden input such as a password.
text: Properties and Methods Text / Label : Text contains the value being edited. Label adds a heading above the input. A labeled TextBox with a border needs at least 5 rows to show the label, separator and input. OnEnter : Called when the user submits the input. This is an Action string, TextBox , receiving the text and the TextBox that submitted it. OnTextChanged : Called when the user edits the text or Clear is called. Assigning Text in C# does not call this callback. EnterHit : A parameterless callback for submission. This is useful when you want to add MXML actions without using the submitted value. Multiline / ReadOnly / MaxLength : Multiline allows line breaks. ReadOnly prevents user edits. MaxLength limits the number of UTF-16 units; 0 means there is no limit. HideCharacters / HiddenCharacter : HideCharacters masks the input. HiddenCharacter sets the mask character, which is * by default. C# Example Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples. C# Copy var control = new TextBox { Label = Display name , Text = Melon listener , Height = 5 , Width = 42 , MaxLength = 64 }; control.OnEnter = (text, input) = input.Label = $ Hello, {text} ; MXML Example App refers to the SettingsModel backend from the Data Binding Guide . Register it with page.BackendObjects.Add("App", model) before compiling. MXML Copy MUIPage ShowBorder= false TextBox Label= Display name Text= Melon listener Height= 5 Width= 42 MaxLength= 64 OnEnter= {App.Submit} / /MUIPage Output Example Example Output: ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐ │Display name │ ├────────────────────────────────────────┤ │Melon listener │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ Keyboard Controls Left / Right, Home / End: Move the cursor; editing/deletion respects text elements. Enter: Submit in single-line mode; insert a newline in multiline mode. Shift+Enter: Submit multiline text. Ctrl+R: Reveal/conceal a focused password; focus loss conceals it. Notes In the MXML example, App.Submit is a public method with the signature void Submit(string text, TextBox input). The data binding guide includes the SettingsModel class used here. To bind the input to a property, set Text="{App.Name}". User edits will then update App.Name. Hidden input is masked in normal CaptureText output, even if the user has revealed it. You must explicitly set includeSensitive=true to include it in a capture. TextBox does not currently provide text selection, clipboard, or autocomplete APIs.
